sections.body: This section introduces RCC curing topics, covered in the following subsections: E-14.1 General, E-14.2 Effect of Moist Curing on Frost Resistance, and E-14.3 Early Loading.
key_points: Introduces curing subsections: general moist curing, frost resistance effect, and early loading restrictions.
sections.applicability: Framing section for RCC curing subsections E-14.1 through E-14.3.

sections.title: E-14.1: General
sections.summary: Explains why RCC's rough/open texture requires at least 7 days of continuous moist curing (spray truck, sprinkler, burlap, or mats), warns about washing away surface fines and managing curing-water runoff, and notes double-rate membrane curing compound/asphalt emulsion as alternatives.
sections.body: The relatively rough or open surface texture of the compacted RCC pavement will tend to dry very quickly. To prevent this, moist curing has been commonly recommended to prevent drying and scaling of the RCC pavement surface. For moist curing, the pavement surface should be kept continuously moist after final rolling for at least seven days by means of a water spray truck, sprinkler (fog spray) system, wet burlap, or cotton mat covering; if burlap mats are used, they should be thoroughly wetted, placed on the RCC pavement so the entire surface and exposed edges are covered, and kept continuously wet. An irrigation sprinkler system has been used to cure RCC pavement on some projects, but caution should be exercised so that the fines in the surface of the RCC pavement are not washed away by excessive pressure, particularly in the first few hours. Curing RCC pavement with water can generate considerable runoff and, if not properly handled, cause erosion or saturation of exposed subgrade. Curing with membrane-forming curing compound and asphalt emulsion applied at double the rates used on conventional concrete have been used successfully.
key_points: RCC's rough, open surface texture dries quickly, so continuous moist curing (spray truck, fog sprinkler, wet burlap, or cotton mats) is recommended for at least 7 days after final rolling.

Irrigation sprinkler curing requires caution to avoid washing away surface fines under excessive pressure, especially in the first few hours; runoff must be managed to avoid erosion or subgrade saturation.
Membrane-forming curing compound and asphalt emulsion, applied at double the rate used on conventional concrete, have also been used successfully.
sections.applicability: Applies to selecting and executing a moist- or membrane-curing method for RCC pavement.

sections.title: E-14.2: Effect of Moist Curing on Frost Resistance
sections.summary: Reports preliminary lab freeze-thaw findings that low-w/cm, extended-moist-cured RCC is more frost resistant, attributed to more complete hydration or reduced permeability.
sections.body: Preliminary results of laboratory freezing and thawing tests indicate that RCC having a sufficiently low w/cm ratio and moist cured for an extended period is more frost resistant. The improved frost resistance may be due to more complete hydration reducing the fractional volume of freezable water at saturation or by reducing the permeability of the RCC, making it more difficult to saturate under wet conditions.
key_points: Preliminary lab freeze-thaw testing indicates low-w/cm RCC with extended moist curing is more frost resistant.
Improved frost resistance may result from more complete cement hydration (less freezable water at saturation) or reduced permeability (harder to saturate).
sections.applicability: Applies to understanding the link between moist curing duration/w/cm and RCC frost resistance.

sections.title: E-14.3: Early Loading
sections.summary: Restricts vehicular traffic from RCCP until curing is complete, allowing only minimal-turn water-spray truck access if absolutely necessary.
sections.body: All vehicular traffic should be kept off the RCCP until the end of the curing period. If it is absolutely necessary, a water-spraying truck may be driven onto the pavement before that age, but any turns must be kept to a minimum; water-spraying trucks or any other traffic should be kept to a minimum.
key_points: All vehicular traffic should be kept off RCCP until curing is complete.
If a water-spraying truck must be driven onto the pavement early, turning maneuvers and overall traffic should be minimized.
sections.applicability: Applies to restricting early traffic loading on RCCP during the curing period.

sections.title: E-15: Quality Control/Assurance
sections.summary: Framing section for RCCP QC/QA subsections: general UFGS framework, QC operations, QA operations, plant tests, field density tests, core sampling, smoothness, surface texture, cylinder/beam fabrication and its method, and inspector duties.
sections.body: This section introduces RCCP quality control/quality assurance topics, covered in the following subsections: E-15.1 General, E-15.2 Quality Control Operations, E-15.3 Quality Assurance Operations, E-15.4 Tests at Plant, E-15.5 Field Density Tests, E-15.6 Obtaining Core Samples, E-15.7 Smoothness, E-15.8 Surface Texture, E-15.9 Cylinder and Beam Fabrication, E-15.10 Method of Cylinder and Beam Fabrication, and E-15.11 Inspectors.
key_points: Introduces QC/QA subsections spanning general requirements, contractor QC and government QA operations, plant/field/core testing, smoothness/texture acceptance, specimen fabrication, and inspector duties.
sections.applicability: Framing section for RCC QC/QA subsections E-15.1 through E-15.11.

sections.title: E-15.1: General
sections.summary: States that the UFGSs provide construction-method requirements and outline the expected QC/QA measures and limits for density, smoothness, thickness, and surface texture.
sections.body: The UFGSs provide requirements on the construction method and outline expected QC and QA measures and limits for density, smoothness, thickness, and surface texture.
key_points: UFGSs establish the construction method requirements and the expected QC/QA measures and limits for density, smoothness, thickness, and surface texture.
sections.applicability: Applies as the overarching QC/QA framework reference (UFGS) for RCCP projects.

sections.title: E-15.2: Quality Control Operations
sections.summary: Lists the contractor's QC responsibilities: aggregate sampling/gradation/quality/moisture testing, plant calibration checks, ASTM D1557 moisture-density tests, nuclear-gauge in-place density/moisture, straightedge smoothness, core sampling, and optional cylinder/beam fabrication.
sections.body: QC operations for DoD RCC pavement projects are the responsibility of the contractor. QC consists of sampling, gradation, quality, and moisture testing of aggregates going into the concrete; checking the plant calibration regularly; conducting moisture-density relationship tests (ASTM D1557) on the fresh RCC; measuring the in-place density and moisture content of the RCC by using a nuclear gauge; checking the smoothness of the finished RCC with a straightedge; taking core samples from the RCC for measurement of density, strength, and thickness; and, if desired, fabricating RCC cylinders and beams.
key_points: QC is the contractor's responsibility, covering aggregate sampling/gradation/quality/moisture testing, regular plant calibration, and ASTM D1557 moisture-density tests on fresh RCC.
QC also includes nuclear-gauge in-place density/moisture measurement, straightedge smoothness checks, and core sampling for density/strength/thickness.
sections.applicability: Applies to defining the contractor's QC testing scope for an RCCP project.

sections.title: E-15.3: Quality Assurance Operations
sections.summary: Lists the government's QA responsibilities (mixture proportions, material quality testing, acceptance testing, random QC duplication) and the lot/payment structure tied to density, smoothness, surface texture, and thickness.
sections.body: QA consists of providing the RCC mixture proportions, testing cementitious materials and aggregates for quality, and testing in-place density, smoothness, surface texture, and thickness for acceptance. QA testing by the government may also consist of randomly duplicating any QC test to determine if consistent results are being obtained. Payment is based on the results of the QA tests (density, smoothness, surface texture, and thickness) for each lot, which represents a day's placement of pavement. If the QA test results show deficiencies in any of these four areas, the payment for the lot is reduced, and the lot is rejected if the deficiency is too great.
key_points: QA covers providing mixture proportions, testing cementitious materials/aggregates for quality, and testing in-place density/smoothness/surface texture/thickness for acceptance.
Government QA may randomly duplicate QC tests to check consistency of results.

Payment for each lot (a day's placement) is based on QA test results in density, smoothness, surface texture, and thickness; deficiencies reduce payment, and a lot is rejected if deficiency is too great.
sections.applicability: Applies to the government's QA testing scope and its role in payment/acceptance decisions for RCCP.

sections.title: E-15.4: Tests at Plant
sections.summary: Describes daily aggregate moisture checks, thrice-daily washed gradation tests (with No. 100 sieve passing determined), and the ASTM C685 washout proportioning check on combined dry ingredients.
sections.body: Moisture contents of the fine and coarse aggregates should be determined daily, as necessary, and appropriate changes made in the amount of mixing water. Washed gradation tests should normally be performed on the combined aggregates three times per day: in the morning, at midday, and in the afternoon; the samples should be taken from the conveyor before the cement or fly ash is added to the combined aggregates. The amount of materials passing the 0.150 mm (No. 100) sieve should be determined during this analysis. Whenever the characteristics of the mixture change or a check on the ingredients is required, a proportioning check can be performed on the combined dry ingredients on samples taken from the conveyor belt between the cement and fly ash hoppers and the pugmill, using a washout test according to procedures in ASTM C685 (paragraph 6.5). By washing the dry ingredients over the 4.75 and 0.150 mm (No. 4 and No. 100) sieves and weighing the material in each size category, the approximate proportions of coarse aggregate, fine aggregate, and cement and fly ash combined may be determined and checked against predetermined limits.
key_points: Aggregate moisture content is checked daily; washed gradation tests on combined aggregates are normally performed 3 times per day (morning, midday, afternoon) from conveyor samples taken before cement/fly ash addition.
Percent passing the 0.150 mm (No. 100) sieve is determined during gradation analysis.

A washout test per ASTM C685 (paragraph 6.5), washing over the 4.75 mm and 0.150 mm (No. 4 and No. 100) sieves, checks combined proportions of coarse aggregate, fine aggregate, and cement+fly ash against predetermined limits whenever mixture characteristics change.
sections.applicability: Applies to plant-level daily/periodic QC testing of aggregate moisture, gradation, and proportioning.

sections.title: E-15.5: Field Density Tests
sections.summary: Specifies ASTM D6938 nuclear gauge density testing frequency (at least 1 per 30 m of lane), test-section-based correction, and re-rolling of deficient areas.
sections.body: Field density tests should be performed on the RCC pavement using a nuclear density gauge operated in the direct transmission mode according to ASTM D6938, with the full-depth reading being used for control and acceptance. At least one field reading should be taken for every 30 m (100 ft) of each paving lane, with readings taken as closely behind the rolling operation as possible. The reading should be adjusted using the correlation determined in the test section construction and checked against a specified density. Areas that indicate a deficient density should be rolled again with the vibratory roller until the specified density is achieved.
key_points: Field density is measured with a nuclear gauge in direct transmission mode per ASTM D6938 (full-depth reading), at least once per 30 m (100 ft) of each paving lane, taken as close behind rolling as possible.
Readings are adjusted using the correlation established during test-section construction and checked against the specified density.
Deficient-density areas are re-rolled with the vibratory roller until the specified density is achieved.
sections.applicability: Applies to production field density testing and acceptance during RCCP construction.

sections.title: E-15.6: Obtaining Core Samples
sections.summary: Describes core-based thickness acceptance testing, requiring the pavement to be at least 5 days old, with 1 random core per sublot for thickness plus additional cores for density/strength as directed.
sections.body: The acceptance criteria for the thickness of the RCC pavement are based on appropriate tests conducted on cores taken from the pavement. Take cores from the pavement when it is no less than five days old. Take one core at a random location selected within each sublot, which is one-fourth the size of a lot, and measure the thickness; take additional cores as determined by the government for density and splitting tensile strength.
key_points: Thickness acceptance is based on cores taken when the pavement is at least 5 days old.
One core is taken at a random location within each sublot (one-fourth of a lot) for thickness measurement; additional cores are taken as directed for density and splitting tensile strength.
sections.applicability: Applies to core sampling procedures used for RCCP thickness, density, and strength acceptance testing.

sections.title: E-15.7: Smoothness
sections.summary: Requires smoothness checking as closely behind the finish roller as possible with correction by the finish roller, with particular attention to fresh/cold joint smoothness, and stresses the roller operator's skill.
sections.body: Do not finish the surface of the RCCP outside the tolerances given in the specifications. Check the smoothness as closely behind the finish roller as possible; correct excessive variations in the surface with the finish roller. Pay particular attention to the smoothness across fresh and cold joints because this is typically a critical area for surface variations. A skilled vibratory roller operator is essential to minimize smoothness problems.
key_points: Surface smoothness must be checked as closely behind the finish roller as possible and corrected immediately with the finish roller if outside tolerance.
Smoothness across fresh and cold joints is a typically critical area requiring particular attention.
A skilled vibratory roller operator is essential to minimize smoothness problems.
sections.applicability: Applies to construction-phase smoothness control and correction for RCC pavement.

sections.title: E-15.8: Surface Texture
sections.summary: Describes the acceptable coarse, void/fissure-textured RCCP surface (resembling asphalt) and lists the surface defects it must be free of.
sections.body: The final surface texture of an RCC pavement resembles that of an asphalt concrete pavement surface: a coarse surface texture with regularly spaced voids and interconnected fissures. The final surface texture should be devoid of surface tears, check cracking, segregation, rock pockets, surface patches, pumped areas, aggregate drag marks, loose aggregate, or exposed aggregate from washed fines.
key_points: RCCP's final surface texture resembles asphalt concrete: a coarse texture with regularly spaced voids and interconnected fissures.
Acceptable surface must be free of tears, check cracking, segregation, rock pockets, surface patches, pumped areas, aggregate drag marks, loose aggregate, or fines-washed exposed aggregate.
sections.applicability: Applies to visual acceptance criteria for finished RCCP surface texture.

sections.title: E-15.9: Cylinder and Beam Fabrication
sections.summary: Encourages fabricating field cylinders/beams as a QC aid complementing coring, requiring a reported correlation to core/sawed-beam strength and density from the test section when used.
sections.body: The fabrication of cylinders and beams during RCCP construction may be specified and is encouraged if not specified. These beams and cylinders complement the coring operation to check RCCP strength and density. When fabricated cylinders and beams are used as a QC aid during construction, determine and report a correlation between their strength and density and those obtained from cores and sawed beams obtained from the test section.
key_points: Field cylinder/beam fabrication during RCCP construction complements coring for checking strength and density and is encouraged even when not specified.
When used as a QC aid, a correlation must be determined and reported between fabricated-specimen strength/density and that of cores/sawed beams from the test section.
sections.applicability: Applies to deciding whether/how to use field-fabricated cylinders and beams as a QC aid.

sections.title: E-15.10: Method of Cylinder and Beam Fabrication
sections.summary: Details field cylinder fabrication (3-layer molds, 3,600 vpm vibration under 9.1 kg surcharge, 8 cylinders per 225 m3, tested per ASTM C496 at 7/14/28/90 days) and field beam fabrication per CRD-C 161 (2-layer molds, 57 kg surcharge, 4 beams per shift, tested per ASTM C78 at 14/28 days).
sections.body: Fabricate cylinders in the field by filling cylinder molds in three equal layers. Each layer is consolidated by vibrating each layer on a vibrating table having a frequency of 3,600 vibrations per minute, under a surcharge of 9.1 kg (20 lb); vibrate each layer until a mortar ring is visible around the entire periphery of the surcharge. Fabricate eight cylinders for every 225 m3 (300 yd3) of RCC placed; test two cylinders each at 7, 14, 28, and 90 days for splitting tensile strength according to ASTM C496. No procedure has been standardized for fabricating RCC beam specimens such as those used to determine concrete flexural strength; however, CRD-C 161 details a procedure that fills beam molds in two layers, each layer consolidated by vibrating on a vibrating table having a frequency of 3,600 vibrations per minute, under a surcharge of 57 kg (125 lb), uniformly distributed over the entire specimen area during molding, with vibration continued until a ring of mortar forms around the complete periphery of the mold. Fabricate four beams during each shift of construction: two to be tested at 14 days and two at 28 days for flexural strength according to ASTM C78.
key_points: Field cylinders are cast in 3 equal layers, each vibrated at 3,600 vpm under a 9.1 kg (20 lb) surcharge until a mortar ring appears; fabricate 8 cylinders per 225 m3 (300 yd3) of RCC placed.
Test 2 cylinders each at 7, 14, 28, and 90 days for splitting tensile strength per ASTM C496.

Beams follow CRD-C 161: filled in 2 layers, each vibrated at 3,600 vpm under a 57 kg (125 lb) surcharge until a mortar ring forms; fabricate 4 beams per shift (2 tested at 14 days, 2 at 28 days) for flexural strength per ASTM C78.
sections.applicability: Applies to the exact procedure for fabricating field QC cylinders and beams from RCC.

sections.title: E-15.11: Inspectors
sections.summary: Assigns at least one inspector each to the plant and jobsite, detailing plant duties (mixing time/consistency checks, coordinating aggregate/gradation/calibration/washout testing) and jobsite duties (moistening, timing, grade control, gaps, rolling, smoothness, texture, thickness, curing, and coordinating gauge/coring/specimen/smoothness testing).
sections.body: Inspections are vital in QC operations. Station at least one inspector at the mixing plant and at the jobsite to ensure a quality pavement is being built. At the mixing plant, check mixing times and spot-check the consistency and appearance of the mix coming out of the plant; the inspector coordinates the aggregate moisture content tests, the gradation tests, calibration of the plant, and washout tests to see that they are performed properly and at the right frequency. At the jobsite, the inspector ensures the base course and cold joints are moistened before the RCC is placed against them and that the RCC is placed and compacted within the proper time limitations; checks the paver operation to ensure proper grade control is continuously maintained and ensures no gaps or discontinuities are left in the pavement before rolling; ensures the roller begins compaction at the proper time and that the proper rolling pattern and number of passes are used; ensures adequate smoothness across joints is achieved and that the surface texture is tight after final rolling; spot-checks the final compacted thickness of the RCCP and corrects when out of tolerance; ensures the curing procedures are implemented as specified; ensures all exposed surfaces of the RCCP are kept moist at all times and that the curing compound, if used, is applied properly and in a continuous fashion. The inspector coordinates the nuclear gauge density test, the coring procedures, cylinder and beam fabrication, and the surface smoothness test to ensure they are performed properly and at the required frequency.
key_points: At least one inspector is stationed at the mixing plant and one at the jobsite.
Plant inspector duties: check mixing times, mix consistency/appearance, and coordinate aggregate moisture, gradation, plant calibration, and washout testing.

Jobsite inspector duties: verify base/cold joint moistening, placement/compaction timing, paver grade control, absence of gaps before rolling, correct roller timing/pattern/passes, joint smoothness, surface texture, compacted thickness, and proper curing (including curing compound application).
Jobsite inspector also coordinates nuclear gauge density tests, coring, cylinder/beam fabrication, and smoothness testing for proper performance and frequency.
sections.applicability: Applies to defining plant and jobsite inspector responsibilities during RCCP construction QC/QA.
